question.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman Britain.
question.text: This structure marked the northern boundary of Roman Britain. It stretches across northern England and is named for the emperor who built it.
question.clue: A birthday invitation was found on one of the Vindolanda tablets, which were unearthed near this structure.

swap.leadin: A period of expansion into Germany under this ruler was ended by defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
swap.text: Name this first Emperor of Rome, who conquered Egypt through victory at the Battle of Actium.
swap.answerHtml: Octavian [or Augustus Caesar or Gaius Octavius; do not accept or prompt on just “Caesar”]
swap.clue: The Second Triumvirate consisted of Antony, Lepidus, and this adopted son of Julius Caesar, who fought a civil war against Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE and became the first Emperor of Rome.

question.text: Hannibal's last battle was this engagement near Carthage, in which he was defeated by Scipio Africanus. At it, Roman and Numidian cavalry scattered Hannibal's lines.
question.clue: The cavalry under Syphax were on the left flank of one commander, who had been ordered home after a loss at Utica.

swap.text: This man succeeded Nerva as emperor and served from 98 to 117. Known for his public building projects, this man is the namesake of a column in Rome commemorating his victory in the Dacian Wars.
swap.clue: This man employed Apollodorus of Damascus to build a namesake forum as well as a bridge across the Danube.

question.leadin: Answer some questions on the Roman Empire during the 1st century.
question.text: Although this emperor ruled for only two years, his time as emperor was consequential. He put an end to the Jewish rebellion, destroyed the Second Temple of Jerusalem, oversaw the completion of the Roman Colosseum, and witnessed the eruption of Mount Vesuvius.
question.clue: This ruler faced a rebellion led by the lute-playing Terentius Maximus, who claimed he was Nero.
question.set: 2023 Politics & History with a side of Memes

swap.leadin: Name the following about a period in Roman history.
swap.text: This emperor earned his sobriquet by convincing the Senate to accord his adoptive father Hadrian divine honors and built a namesake wall across Scotland in 142 AD.
swap.answerHtml: Antoninus Pius [or Titus Aurelius Fulvius Boionius Arrius Antoninus; or Titus Aelius Caesar Antoninus; or Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius]
swap.clue: During the rule of this emperor, the third-largest complex of Roman baths was built in Carthage.

question.leadin: Fans of this sport destroyed the Baths of Zeuxippus during one revolt.
question.text: Name this sport whose greens and blues factions attempted to install Hypatius as emperor while chanting "Victory!" in the Nika Riots.
question.answerHtml: chariot racing [or chariot races; prompt on partial answer]
question.clue: In Constantinople, this sport took place in the Hippodrome, while in Rome, it was held in the Circus Maximus.

swap.leadin: These officials had no imperium and no lictor bodyguards, although Domitian declared himself a "perpetual" one.
swap.text: Name this office of the Roman Republic that was responsible for maintaining public morals, and gave its name to the modern act of filtering certain information out of documents.
swap.clue: Only former consuls could be named to this powerful office, which determined eligibility for voting and oversaw public morals laws.

question.leadin: Identify these regions subject to military incursions by Roman forces.
question.text: Decebalus's raids from this region prompted Domitian to launch the first of two namesake wars, whose second incarnation saw Trajan subjugate this region bounded by the Danube and the Carpathians. Its capital was at Sarmizegetusa.
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.text: Tarquinius Superbus fled to this king of Clusium, whose campaign to reinstall the king was foiled by the determination of Mucius Scaevola.
swap.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

question.leadin: To skirt provisions on burials, these people were sometimes enclosed in underground chambers within the pomerium with a loaf of bread and a lamp.
question.text: Name this group of six priestesses who tended a perpetual fire and enjoyed rights such as property ownership, but obeyed a strict vow of chastity.
question.clue: According to Plutarch, these people were punished by being sealed in a chamber near the Colline Gate with only limited food and water.

swap.text: St Isidore aided in the conversion of Visigothic Spain to Catholicism. The Visigoths had earlier followed this doctrine, which asserted that the Son was subordinate to the Father, and which was condemned at the Council of Nicaea.
swap.clue: The emperor Constantius espoused this belief, leading to its further condemnation at the First Council of Constantinople.

question.leadin: Name some members of Wikipedia's illustrious list of sexually active popes.
question.text: A scene in the Book of Matthew describes Jesus healing this man's mother-in-law, clearly implying that he is married. This man is traditionally considered the first pope.
question.clue: Piux IX installed a statue of this first pope in his namesake basilica in the Vatican. As an apostle this man denied Jesus three times.

swap.leadin: According to Herodian, Elagabalus was murdered at an entrance to this system, where Nero allegedly dumped the bodies of street hermits whom he drunkenly killed.
swap.text: Name this system commissioned by Tarquinius Priscus and built by reclaiming the swamps around the Roman Forum. Marcus Agrippa renovated this system and allegedly rode through it as a demonstration.
swap.answerHtml: Roman sewer system [or sewage system; accept drainage system; or sanitation system; or plumbing system; accept Cloaca Maxima; prompt on waste management or water management or wastewater management; prompt on Cloaca]

question.text: Ruling from 535-510 BCE this last of the seven kings of Rome was a tyrant. He was deposed by Lucius Brutus after his son Sextus raped the virtuous Lucretia.
question.clue: This ruler took refuge with Aristodemus of Cumae after a battle in which Castor and Pollux purportedly fought against him.

swap.leadin: The third man who held this title presided over the destruction of Alba Longa.
swap.text: Name this title legendarily held by seven men. The final man in this post, known as the "Proud," was supposedly overthrown shortly after raping a woman named Lucretia.
swap.clue: One of these people tried to retake power at the Battle of Lake Regillus and was responsible for constructing the Cloaca Maxima, while another constructed a gate that was open during wartime and shut during peace.

question.text: An earlier defeat of Pompey was to this man who set up an independent little state in Spain. This man also brought the pain to Metellus and made Pompey cry back to Rome for help. This man was finally killed by some of his pompous henchmen.
question.clue: Along with his lieutenant Hirtuleius, he overthrew the governor Quintus Metellus Pius, and then was joined by Marcus Perpenna, though Perpenna eventually had this man murdered at a banquet.

swap.leadin: According to its first line, this book "is a study of social and cultural change."
swap.text: Name this book by the historian Peter Brown. This book describes how the title period of Mediterranean history between 200 CE and 700 CE differs from "classical" civilization, as it is traditionally defined.

question.text: Curzio Inghirami botched his staged discoveries of Etruscan "scariths" by using paper instead of this material. The Zagreb Book is an Etruscan text written on this material that was found wrapped around an Egyptian mummy.
question.answerHtml: linen [or flax; accept Liber Linteus, Libri lintei, or linen rolls; prompt on textiles, fabric, or synonyms]

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman mosaics.
swap.text: The largest collection of Roman mosaics in the world can be found in this villa in Sicily, which includes the "Chamber of the Ten Maidens" and which features a mosaic titled "The Little Hunt".
swap.clue: This villa in Sicily, which has been identified as the retirement palace of Maximian. It is home to the largest collection of surviving Roman mosaics anywhere, with over 37,000 square feet of figurative floor mosaics.
